iut_type: Profile test report internal QA review (DensoTen project)
customer_question: (Internal) During second-level review of a profile test report, several issues were found: a test item (HFP/HF/ACC) was performed both by Allion and by the customer with different PTS tool versions, and only one is referenced in the report — which one should take precedence? Should the non-referenced version's data be deleted and the report regenerated? Also, several test dates in the report don't match the underlying test logs (off by exactly one month), and some profile version numbers in the report (MAP, PBAP) don't match what's marked True in the test logs.
question_variants: When the same test item is performed redundantly by both the lab and the customer with different tool versions, which result should the official report use?
Do discrepancies between report dates/version numbers and the underlying test logs need to be corrected before finalizing?
actual_issue: A second-level reviewer found that the draft profile test report for a DensoTen project contained an unresolved conflict between Allion's own and the customer's redundantly-performed test results for the same test item (using different tool versions), along with several apparent date and version-number discrepancies between the report's stated values and the underlying raw test logs.
plain_english_explanation: When a test item has been performed by both Allion and the customer with different tool versions, the report should reference whichever result the reviewer can take full ownership and responsibility for — generally Allion's own directly-performed result — rather than defaulting to whichever happens to be currently referenced; if the non-selected version's data isn't needed in the final report, the related content should be removed and the report regenerated to ensure internal consistency. Separately, every date and version-number value appearing in a finalized report must be independently verified against the underlying raw test logs before report finalization, since reviewers identified multiple date discrepancies (consistently off by exactly one month, suggesting a systematic data-entry error) and at least two profile version-number mismatches (MAP and PBAP) that needed correction to ensure the report accurately reflects the actual testing performed.
consultant_answer: Please record in the report whichever version of the test item Allion can take full responsibility for, and if the other version's content isn't going to be used, remove it and regenerate the report for consistency.
decision_logic: When a test report references a result that Allion did not directly produce (or that conflicts with a result Allion did produce), the report should prioritize whichever result Allion can stand fully behind, and any unused redundant test data should be removed via regeneration rather than left inconsistently referenced; separately, every date and version field in a draft report must be cross-checked against the underlying raw test logs as a standard second-level review step, since systematic data-entry errors (like a consistent one-month date offset) can otherwise go unnoticed.
final_recommendation: Establish a standard second-level report review checklist that explicitly includes cross-checking every date and version-number field against raw test logs, and define a clear precedence rule (lab-performed results take priority for which the lab can take responsibility) for any test item performed redundantly by both the lab and the customer.
risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting a final report with unresolved redundant-test-result conflicts or unverified date/version discrepancies could result in a certification record that doesn't accurately reflect the actual testing performed, creating a problem if the report is ever audited or challenged.
